clips.text: [flat, bored] Sector clear. [exhales] Keep moving.
[low, firm] Check the corners... keep your spacing.
[alert, quiet] Heard that. Checking it.
[whispers] Hold here. I'll take a look.
[shouting] Contact! Closing in!
[shouting, urgent] Move up! Cover the flank!
[grunts in pain] Agh-- I'm hit!
[through gritted teeth] Still in it!
[pained, strained] I'm down... keep moving!
[shouting] Detail's gone! Fall back, fall back!
[angry] We lost one! Close the gap!
[calm, quiet] Lane is covered.
[calm] Clear sightline. Holding.
[whispers] Heard something... holding my angle.
[focused, low] Movement at the edge. Checking.
[cold, steady] Target marked. Taking the shot.
[firm] Keep them in the open.
[sharp inhale] Winged-- still up.
[pained] Lost the angle. Moving.
[strained, fading] I'm out... cover the lane.
[tense] Position lost. Breaking contact.
[grim] One down. Watch their lane.
[restless] Eyes forward, eyes forward.
[impatient] Don't bunch up.
[eager] Something moved! I'm on it.
[excited whisper] Cover me. I'll flush it out.
[shouting] Rushing! Get clear!
[yelling, aggressive] I'm going through!
[grunts] Keep going!
[out of breath, defiant] Not stopping!
[gasping] Can't... keep moving!
[panicked shouting] We're overrun! Moving back!
[shouting] They're down! Don't stop here!
[deep, slow] Holding the door.
[gruff] Stay behind the armor.
[low growl] Noise. Nobody runs past me.
[firm] Watch the gap. I'll hold.
[booming] Suppressing! Stay behind me!
[shouting] Keep your heads DOWN!
[grunts] Taking hits.
[groans] That one got through.
[heavy breathing] I'm down-- the door's open!
[grim] Line's broken. Pulling back.
[angry, low] Lost one. Get behind me.
[muttering] Kit is ready.
[casual] Connections look good.
[curious] Could be a short... checking.
[quietly] Keep watch while I check this.
[shouting] Contact! Cover me!
[stressed] I need room to work!
[shouting] Drone out! Cover me!
[focused] Drone's live. Watch your fire.
[strained, working] Hold them off-- I'm fixing it!
[urgent] Checking the pad. Cover me.
[pained laugh] Tools first... then me.
[wincing] I'm hit. Kit's still working.
[weak] I'm down... save the kit.
[panicked] They're all gone! Falling back deeper!
[desperate] Lost another! We need to move!
[calm, soft] All quiet.
[gentle] Keep a dressing where you can reach it.
[worried] That didn't sound good.
[cautious] Checking. Stay in sight.
[shouting] Stay low! Wounded need cover!
[urgent] Cover the wounded!
[soothing] Hold still... I've got you.
[calm, focused] Pressure on. Keep breathing.
[grunts] Medic's hit-- still working.
[pained] I can wait. Cover the patient.
[strained, quiet] I'm down... self-treating.
[shaken] No one left to pull out. Falling back!
[sad, heavy] We've lost them. Stay together.
[nervous] I'm with you. [whispers] Don't leave me.
[shaky breath] Just keep going... I'm right here.
[anxious] I-- I'll stay put. Be quick.
[reluctant] Here? All right... hurry back.
[terrified whisper] They're coming... please...
[panicked] I can hear them! We have to go!
[crying out] Ah-- don't let them take me!
[pained, pleading] I'm hurt... please, wait!
[bored, flat] Checkpoint secure. Eyes on the road.
[firm] Nobody crosses to the tower. Those are the orders.
[alert] Movement by the wire. Checking.
[low, tense] Hold... something is out there.
[shouting] Contact! Open fire!
[commanding shout] Intruder at the checkpoint! Take him down!
[grunts in pain] I'm hit!
[shouting, pained] Medic! MEDIC!
[gasping] Man down... hold the line...
[urgent shouting] Too many! Fall back to the tower road!
[angry] We lost one! Keep firing!
[sighs, lazy] Quiet day. [chuckles] Too quiet for my liking.
[muttering] Anyone comes sniffing round my scrap... they pay.
[suspicious] Eh? Who's there?
[gruff] Heard something by the junk. Go look.
[laughs, shouting] Get him, boys! Rookie's got loot!
[aggressive yell] Light him up!
[angry, pained] Agh! You little rat!
[groans] He got me!
[weak, bitter] Ugh... not like this...
[panicked] Forget the loot! RUN!
[furious] They got one of ours! Make him pay!
[warm, dry] Lead the way, rookie. I've got your back.
[calm] Right behind you. [serious] Mind the anomalies.
[tired sigh] I'll hold here. Don't wander off too far.
[dry chuckle] Fine, I'll wait. Shout if it turns bad.
[urgent] Mutants! Get behind me!
[whispers] Something is moving in the grass... careful.
[groans] Gah... I'm bleeding.
[strained, stubborn] Still breathing. Keep going.
[low, menacing] Saw that.
[whispers, cold] I saw you. Stay put.
[low, firm] Check the lockers.
[quiet, focused] Let's see what's in here.
[shouting] Got you! Out!
[startled, angry shout] Out! Now!
[sighs, irritated] Nothing. Back to it.
[tired, annoyed] Lost him. Stay sharp.
[whispers] I saw that.
[cold, quiet] Saw you go in. Don't move.
[calm, low] Lockers. Clearing them one by one.
[quiet, focused] Let's see what's behind this door.
[sharp, cold] There you are. Out.
[sharp shout] Got you! Hands where I can see them!
[flat, tired] Nothing. Just the vents.
[irritated, quiet] Lost him. Watching the lanes.
[eager whisper] Oh, I saw that.
[quiet, grinning] Saw you. Nowhere to run now.
[impatient] Lockers! Rip them open!
[eager, low] Come on... which one are you in?
[yelling, aggressive] Got you! Out!
[shouting] Gotcha! Move, move!
[frustrated groan] Nothing! Waste of time.
[irritated, out of breath] Lost him. He's still out there.
[low growl] I saw that.
[deep, slow, menacing] Saw you climb in.
[gruff] Lockers. Open them up.
[deep, slow] Let's see what's hiding in here.
[booming] Found you! Get out!
[shouting, angry] Out! NOW!
[tired sigh] Just the pipes. Back to the door.
[gruff, irritated] He slipped us. Eyes open.
[quietly, amused] Oh... I saw that.
[muttering] Saw that. Bad place to hide.
[muttering] Better check these lockers.
[curious, quiet] What have we got in here...
[startled shout] Whoa-- got you!
[startled, angry] Out! Now!
[sighs] Pipes knocking again. Back to work.
[irritated mutter] Lost him. Keep watch.
[quiet, cold] I saw that.
[soft, ominous] I saw you. Come out slowly.
[cautious] Checking the lockers.
[nervous, quiet] Easy... let's see what's in here.
[sharp, startled] There you are! Out!
[shouting] Out! Hands up!
[tired sigh] Nothing. Just nerves.
[uneasy] Lost him. Stay together.
[low, firm] Saw that.
[quiet, menacing] I saw you. Stay where you are.
[firm] Search the lockers. All of them.
[low, tense] Let's see what's in here.
[commanding shout] Got you! Step out!
[shouting] Out! On the ground!
[bored, flat] Nothing. Back to the checkpoint.
[irritated] Lost him. Eyes on the road.
[chuckles, quiet] Oh, I saw that.
[low, amused] Saw that, rookie. Stay put.
[gruff] Check the lockers, boys.
[suspicious muttering] What have we got in here, eh?
[shouting, gleeful] Got you, rookie! Out!
[aggressive yell] Out! Now!
[sighs, lazy] Nothing. Just rats.
[irritated grumble] Slippery little rat... keep your eyes open.
[warm, tired] Good to see you back in one piece.
[wary, low] Easy now. Keep it slow.
[sharp, tense] Lower that. Now.
[angry] Hey! Watch where you are shooting!
[shouting] That is it! Put him down!
[desperate, breathless] Enough! We are done, we are done!
[muttering] Another one. Keep your hands where I can see them.
[nervous] Do not point that at me.
[yelling] He turned on us! Fire!
[panicked] Stop! Please, I have got nothing left!
[calm, quiet] You are not one of them. Good.
[calm, firm] Put the weapon down, friend.
[sharp] So that is how it is. Take him.
[shaking] Let me see to my men. Please.
[restless] Who is that? Oh. You again.
[restless, sharp] Gun down! Gun down!
[shouting] Liar! Light him up!
[sobbing, frantic] I do not want to die out here!
[smirking] The toll is still waiting, my friend.
[friendly, laughing] Hey! Our supplier!
[threatening, low] Point that somewhere else.
[yelling] Cheat! Get him, boys!
[panicked] Take everything! Just take it, it is yours!
[panicked, shouting] Fall back! We cannot hold this!
[slow, gravelly] Another one through the wire. [sighs] Sit, warm your hands. You came for work, or for answers?
[low, serious] A courier went north to the old fuel station three days ago, with our relay code. He never came back. Bring me his PDA.
[dry chuckle] Shells. A bed by the fire. And nobody here shoots you in the back. [pause] Out here, that is a fortune.
[quiet, grave] The plant burned, and the sky kept the ash. Then the storms started. When the siren goes, get under a roof. And stay there.
[bitter] Cleanup men. Sent in to tidy us away, then forgotten. They're starving at the old mine. They'll talk, if you keep your gun down.
[moved, quiet] Then he got further than most. The code still opens the transmitter on the east ridge. [firm] Tell the world we are still here.
[tense, clipped] That's close enough. Gun low. Hands where I can see them. [beat] What do you want?
[low] Then pass. Stay off the headframe. [uneasy] Something lives in the lift shaft. It eats the lamps first.
[tired, cold] I know what they sent us in for. Eleven of us came. Four are left. [threatening, quiet] Say it again, and you make it five.
[disbelieving laugh] Out? [pause, hopeful] If that tower can reach anyone at all, we walk you there ourselves. Lead the way.
[cocky] Whoa, whoa. The yard's ours. You want through? You pay the toll.
[sly] Something worth more than your boots. The soldiers keep a supply crate by their hut. Bring me that, and we are friends.
[menacing, amused] Then turn around. Or the boys turn you into scrap.
[delighted whistle] Now that's manners. Go on through. Nobody in this yard touches you.
[calm, measured] Intake detail. Report.
[tired, uneasy] Intake holding, sir. We heard the great door go.
[cold, unhurried] Then someone opened it. Sweep the booths. Anyone without a band is exposed.
[reluctant, quiet] Copy. Booths. Move.
[quiet, precise] And Intake. If it is one of ours, it is still exposed.
[weak, wary, short of breath] Don't. I'm not going to shoot you. [winces] I can't lift it.
[bitter, quiet] The Investigator. Company man. Came down the service lift at three forty, and every radio's been his since. [pause] He doesn't count us. He counts what we've seen.
[haunted, low] Booth sweep at Medical. He said treat them as exposed. [pause] They were nurses. I stopped following orders about then. [dry, pained] So did my leg.
[tired] West. The clearance desk's in there. He was in Records an hour ago, reading cards. [uneasy] Looking for somebody.
[quiet, unhurried, reading] Every card from Energy Diagnostics. Bag them.
[flat, tired] Sir.
[calm, matter-of-fact] The rest of this floor can burn with the building.
[softly, almost to himself] Not this one. [pause] This one comes with me.
[even, unhurried] Medical detail. The screening floor is closed. Anyone walking it is exposed.
[hollow, tired] Sir, we did the booths. [pause] There's nobody left to walk it.
[dry, without warmth] Then you will not be busy.
[pleasant, unhurried public-address voice] Tier two staff... to the intake desk.
[warm, upbeat newsreel narrator] Welcome to Energy Research. [proudly] Your work powers the world!
[bright, reassuring] Every shift below brings light above. [cheerfully] Wear your band.
[breathless, scared, low] Stop. Don't. [shaky] I've got two rounds... and a radio that won't stop talking.
[quiet and fast, glancing over his shoulder] He counts the radios on the hour. I walk, he hears it. [steadier] But I'm not raising this at you. [grim] Whatever he says next.
[hollow, quiet] Us. [swallows] He said they were exposed. They were reading the counts out loud... [bitter, barely above a whisper] so somebody stopped them reading.
[flat, exhausted] Nine tier threes. Ten to three. [uneasy, quieter] Something's been knocking since four.
[into his radio, voice tight, lying] Nobody's walked it, sir. [a little too quickly] I'd have seen.
[faint, feverish whisper] ...keep the lights on. [pleading] They don't get up... while the lights are on.
[urgent, hushed] Shots in triage. Somebody's moving in triage.
[calm, final] Triage is closed. [beat] Leave it.
[uneasy pause] ...Copy. [quietly] Leaving it.
[calm, measured] Imaging detail. Report.
[slower, patient, a little colder] Imaging detail.
[quiet, unbothered] Log them with the tier threes.
[calm, almost satisfied] Ward C is dark.
[soft, cold] Leave it dark. [beat] They know what to do.
[calm, clipped public-address announcement] Caution. Field activity at the rim. Stand clear of the rail.
[hushed, unnerved] Sweep Two. They're stood up behind the shutters. [sharp breath] The visitors. [whispers] All of them.
[shouting, panicked] Contact! Visitors' rail!
[cold, unhurried] Then put them down. [beat] Nobody leaves the ring wearing a pass.
[weary but firm] That's far enough. Weapon down and we've no quarrel. [tired, dry] We've no anything, any more.
[bitter] Him. The Investigator. [flat, reciting orders] Hold the ring, nobody up from Containment. [quieter] Nobody's come up. Not since B went.
[matter-of-fact, low] Shielding detail's in the corridor. Two men, still on his orders. Past them, Experimental Power... then Conversion.

[low and careful, a man who has done the sums] Somebody had Conversion taken off the containment feed at half two. B's fields went quarter of an hour later. [beat] Put it back and the intake doors run again.
[even, measured] Detail nine. Hold the ring. Nothing comes up from Containment.
[tired] Copy. [hesitant] Sir, there's nothing left down there to come up.
[flat, cold] Then hold it... anyway.
[cold, precise] Shielding detail. Anything that comes west from the ring, you burn.
[strained, frightened] Sir. We've got one mag each. [voice cracking] The wall's moving.
[dry] Then be accurate.
[calm, automated announcement] Conversion output on the containment feed. Intake fields on main power. Doors released.
[tense, low, steady] Gun down, stay out of our line, and we never saw each other. [beat] That door's all we're here for.
[grim, quiet] Kessler's detail went in... at TWO. Feed dropped at quarter past and the door held. [pause] We hear them on the radio. [bitter] Not to us.
[gruff, giving directions] Conversion lab. Up the gallery, round the ring, west. Somebody has to turn its output to containment. [flat] Not us.
[calm, clinical] Intake detail. A contract security officer is loose in your sector. Female, armed, no clearance. [beat] Detain her.
[exasperated, tired] Sir, we're four men on a door. We can't hold it AND chase a guard.
[cold] Then hold the door.
[long pause, resigned] ...Copy.
[calm, unhurried] Intake detail. Door B has its feed. Nobody goes through it. [quiet] Her least of all.
[reluctant] ...Copy. [apologetic but firm] Sorry, miss. Hands where we can see them.
[gravelly, bitter] So the hub got its power and not us. [hard] Hands where I can see them.
[low, haunted] Every cell let go at two. Same second. [pause] Kessler held the inner door... and the door held him.
[weary] Doc can't walk. And you heard the radio. [dry, bleak] Out there we're exposed. In here we're just stuck.
[urgent, low] West is where it started. Don't. The aisle's grown shut; out our door and round is the only way south. [steadier] Handling floor, then the theater. The spur east loops back to A.
[calm, clinical] Intake detail. Containment B detail is compromised. [beat] Treat them as exposed.
[angry, holding it together] Sir, this is B. We're not exposed. We're shut in. [voice catching] Kessler's dead.
[quiet, without sympathy] Then you know what exposed looks like.
[defeated, quiet] He's not coming. Nobody's coming. [gently] Sit down, Doc.
[gruff, to her] You. Anything comes through that hole while you're here... we've got it.
[hoarse, steady] We've been on this door since three. Raise it and we go down with you... or ahead of you. [beat] Your choice.
[low, uneasy] Deep research. Bore samples. Whatever they were digging toward. [pause] He says nothing goes down. [quieter] He didn't say why.
[measured, firm] Emergency detail. Hold the barricade. Nothing goes down to Deep Research.
[tired, hoarse] Sir, we've held it four hours. There's nobody left out there to keep out.
[soft, cold] Then you are keeping... something in.
[quiet, the penny dropping] Oh. [to himself] He means us.
[calm, brisk] Geophysics detail. Burn the charts and fall back to the drill.
[uneasy] Sir, nobody has come back up from the interface since three.
[cold, slow] Then... you will be the first.
[quiet, decided] You heard him. [firm] We're not going.
[quiet, unhurried] Hold the readers. Nobody follows me down.
[hesitant, respectful] Sir. The drill team has asked for relief twice.
[mild, almost kind] They will be relieved when the seam is quiet.
[softly, final] The hoist stays at the bottom.
[calm, measured] Mine head. She is at the interface.
[quiet, final] Close it.
[clipped, businesslike] Mine head to control. Gate is down and pinned.
[uncertain, lowering his voice] Sir, there are lamps lit on the survey drift.
[pause, uneasy] They are not ours.
[calm, almost tender] They are hers. Leave them lit.
[softly, slowly, with certainty] She is going... where we are going.
[whispered from the floor, relief cracking through] Are they still down there? You're not his. He sends two.
[bitter, tired, handing it over] Countersign. Thirty years for that word. Take it. The desk reads it as me, and I'm already on his list.
[flat, not meeting your eye] Energy Diagnostics. Tier two. Medical put her in red at two fifteen. He asked for her by name. I didn't ask why.
[quiet, a confession he has rehearsed] The board's list. I chaired the board. Ninety days between screenings. It read well in a quarter.
[low and even, a man doing a job] Face the door. Hands on your head.
[shaking, pleading, fast] I switched the tube off. That's all I did.
[into the handset, deadpan] Imaging. One more for the tier threes.
[hissed over his shoulder, backing off] Kath. Kath, there's someone in the corridor.
[muffled through the door, firm] Leave it. That's not one of theirs. Let her in.
[low, urgent, still in theatre voice] Shut it behind you. Is it dark all the way up the ward?
[brisk, unclipping it from her lanyard] He gave me the spare so I could fetch him between cases. Take it. Throw the transfer and the ward lights come back.
[defiant, then quieter at the end] I cut her straps at half five and left OBS 6 open. I wasn't scrubbing for her. She walked out like she knew the way.
[matter-of-fact, a warning she means] Forty. Certified on the table, still talking. Drawer nine. If the store's tubes go, he's up. Don't stop in the west aisle.
[to the wall, under his breath, after the order] ...Accurate.
[whispered, crouched, not looking up] Don't. My magazine's in the brick. I'm off his radio. Keep your voice down; he settles while somebody talks.
[fond, almost proud] Harris. Fitter. Taught me to lay brick, course on course. He still goes to the shelves. He still knows where everything is.
[rising panic, cut off] ...Harris? No. No, he's listening. Harris, it's me. It's-
[low, quick, a bargain] Their board shut it. The repeater's on that wall, locked to the board, and the locks on this detail are a screwdriver. I'll throw it. You go west and you never saw me.
[flat, already turned back to Harris] Done. Go on. Don't come back through here with that light on.
[tired, certain] And leave him? He'd come looking. He always comes looking for whoever had the radio on.
[gruff, winded, hurt] Two cans. Same as last night.
[dry, careful] Tell your sergeant thank you.
[half a laugh, no humour] Tell him yourself. He won't hear it either.
[weary, matter-of-fact] Conversion, night shift. What's left of it. Nine gives us the fire. Not the door.
[confession, steady] I.I. had the output off containment at half two. I pulled the feeder handle off the bank myself. Holt took the spare back down at three to put it right.
[quiet, an instruction] On the floor by column four, I'd think. He crossed on the light. You cross on the dark.
[handing it over, relieved] Then you'll want this. The bank's feeder handle. I've carried it since half two like it was mine. The bank throws every four seconds: go in on the dark.
[curt, looking away] Don't thank me. Put it on the bank.
[bitter, low] Anyone up from below is exposed, the sergeant says. We came up from Conversion, not Containment. He doesn't ask which.
[flat, careful, a man giving his name at a gate, muffled by glass] Dawes. Peter Dawes. Bench tech, B shift.
[quieter, pleading under the calm, muffled by glass] Dawes. Write it down. Somebody write it down.
[running, breathless, terrified, shouted up the lab] Help me! I did what he said, I boxed them!
[level, tired, not raised] Doctor. Stop.
[into a handset, flat, after a pause, looking at her] Materials. One more. The lab's clear but the two of ours.
[whispered fast, shaking, from the floor] Shut the door. Did he see you? The one who did Hale.
[low, bitter, holding it together] Materials. He boxed the D-series for the lift, like he was told. Then he asked where the lift goes.
[wry, unsure, a little hope] Mendez and the boy. They drink my coffee. They might take my word.
[dry, frightened humour] Past that? I'll keep the bed warm. Go on.
[shouted through a door, voice cracking] Mendez! The guard's with me. She's not his. Let her by!
[reluctant, to his partner, across the lab] ...Doc says let her by. Lower it.
[guarded, rifle low, worn out] That's close enough. We hold this corridor. Not you. Say what you want.

[matter-of-fact briefing, darkening at the end] Core hall. Shed the load on the gallery, then isolate on the pit floor. Fifty seconds between. Something came up the feed at four. It takes whoever's alone.
[quiet decision, half a smile at the last line] Our board's on the dump bank's line. It trips, I throw it back from here. Every time, while you're down. Then I forget I did.
[weary, giving up something] Take it. Rounds on the bunk. Nothing left down here to shoot at that shoots back.
[clipped, over a handset, urgent] Bank's tripped. Throwing it back. Go.
[screams in agony] AAAGH--!
[choking, gurgling, dying] Hhk... ghh... hhh.
[cries out in sudden pain] Aah-- AAH!
[wheezing, fading out] Hhh... no... hhh...
[sharp, agonized cry] Nngh-- AAGH!
[gurgling, last breath] Ghh... hhh.
[deep roar of pain] RRAAGH!
[heavy, dying groan] Uunnghh... hhh.
[screams, then chokes] AAAH-- hhk...
[weak, fading groan] Ohh... hhh...
[yells in agony] AARGH! NO--
[gasping, choking] Hhk-- hhk... hh.
[terrified scream] NO-- AAAH!
[weak, crying, fading] Please... hhh...
[agonized scream] AAAGH!
[dying gasp] Hhh... uhh.
[guttural scream] GRAAAH--!
[rattling last breath] Hhhhh... ghh.
[screams in terror and pain] AAAAH--!
[agonized, choking] Ghh-- ahh... hhh.
[cries out, then gurgles] AH-- oh God-- hhk...
[short pained cry as he falls] Unh--!
[grunts in pain] Ngh!
[pained gasp] Agh--!
[yelps in pain] Ow-- ahh!
[screams] AAAAH--!
[agonized, choking] Hhk... no... hhh.
[terrified scream, cut short] NO-- AAH--
[sharp pained gasp] Ah--!
[cries out in pain] Ow-- ahh!
[gasping, weak] Command... I'm hit... can't feel my...
[choking, faint] Tell them... it came out of the walls...
[struggling to breathe] Man down... he's right... [gasps]
[faint, fading] Don't... send anyone... else.
[heavy, labored] I'm done... the door's yours...
[gasping] Keep... moving... don't stop for...
